title: Rooms in Rust from the interior kit: 2 m modules with real reveals, 2k scans per room, trims, props, hero models and photographic decals, never untextured boxes
note: Build an indoor level from docs/examples/interior-kit: copy assets/kit, place its 2 m modules, props and hero models, wear it with its decals, never boxes.
intent: Untextured boxes and one tinted scan everywhere read as a prototype. Copy docs/examples/interior-kit/assets/kit/ to assets/kit/ and lay the level out in 2 m wall modules as that example's game.rs does: wall, wall-window or wall-door (the opening's sides are its reveals), each painted face with its -paint coat and -trims; windows with window-frame, window-sill, window-sash, window-glass or window-glass-broken and a grille; door-frame and door; beam, light-fitting with light-tube, radiator, desk, chair, teacher-desk, blackboard, debris. Draw each with frame.model_with and its role's material: 2k CC0 scans at their real size (.with_world_uv, stochastic tiling, macro variation) for plaster, paint, floor and concrete, a dado colour and a floor per room; kit/trim_*.jpg and kit/props_*.jpg for the rest. hero/lockers and hero/car-shell keep their own materials: frame.model. Give radiator, desk, chair and the sunburst grille their -lod1 with Model::with_levels. Colliders come from the plan. Wear is kit/decals: peel_edge under the dado rail, leak under sills, grime_base along the floor, ceiling_stain overhead, posters, chalk on the slate.
port: The facet that owns the level's layout owns the module plan, its colliders and its probes; a facet that dresses a room places the kit's props and decals and tags them.

evidence.source: src/game-template-rust/docs/examples/interior-kit (the kit, its script and a corridor and classroom built from it)
evidence.note: 42 one-material GLBs on a 2 m grid, two generated hero models, 2k trim and props sheets from CC0 scans, and decals keyed from generated photographs; one plan draws, collides and wears them.
Material::with_world_uv and with_stochastic_tiling keep a scan at its real size on any piece; decals lay wear onto a surface.
A room is built, not boxed: greybox, scans, then the interior kit's modules and dressing.
